result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.trav_reverse_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse to reverse edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L8586-L8648){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.trav_reverse_edge(add_to_selection=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Traverse to reverse edges](/assets/graphs/trav-reverse-edge.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: two edges are selected in the accent color, C to D and A to C; C and D are also joined by a second edge from D back to C. Right: after trav_reverse_edge() only D to C is selected, the reverse of C to D; A to C has no reverse edge, so it contributes nothing." width="100%"} From the currently selected edges, finds the reverse edges. For each selected edge `A->B`, looks for the corresponding edge `B->A`. Only works with directed graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [add_to_selection]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, adds reverse edges to the current selection. If `False`, replaces the selection with reverse edges only. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} With `add_to_selection=False` (the default), the selection is replaced entirely by each edge's reverse. Selecting only the `A->B` edge and traversing lands on `B->A` instead: ::: {#3fee8aab .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="A") # reverse edge ) a_to_b = graph.find_edge_ids(source="A", target="B") graph.select_edges_by_id(a_to_b) graph.trav_reverse_edge() graph.get_selected_edge_ids() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [2] ``` ::: ::: With `add_to_selection=True`, the reverse edges are added alongside the originals instead of replacing them -- so both `A->B` and `B->A` end up selected: ::: {#41afd866 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.select_edges_by_id(a_to_b) graph.trav_reverse_edge(add_to_selection=True) len(graph.get_selected_edge_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
